hints: Start with the $40 \text{ cm}^{3}$ of glycerine of density $1.3 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ and find its mass using $m = \rho V$.
Let the added water volume be $V$ in $\text{cm}^{3}$, so its mass is $1.0V$ in $\text{g}$ and the mixture has total mass $52+V$ and total volume $40+V$.
Set mixture density $(52+V)/(40+V)$ equal to $1.1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ and solve the linear equation for $V$.
walkthrough: Find the mass of glycerine: $m_g = \rho_g V_g = 1.3 \times 40 = 52 \text{ g}$.
Let added water volume be $V \text{ cm}^{3}$. Then water mass is $m_w = 1.0 \times V = V \text{ g}$.
Total mass is $m = 52 + V$ in $\text{g}$ and, with no volume change on mixing, total volume is $V_{total} = 40 + V$ in $\text{cm}^{3}$.
Multiply out: $52 + V = 44 + 1.1V$, so $8 = 0.1V$ and $V = 80 \text{ cm}^{3}$. This is option D.

options.A: Too small to lower the density from $1.3 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ to $1.1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ when starting with $40 \text{ cm}^{3}$ of glycerine.
options.B: Gives a mixture density well above $1.1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ because the mass of glycerine still dominates the total mass.
options.C: Close to the glycerine volume but does not satisfy $(52+V)/(40+V)=1.1$ for $V$ in $\text{cm}^{3}$.
options.D: With $V=80 \text{ cm}^{3}$ total mass is $52+80=132 \text{ g}$ and total volume is $120 \text{ cm}^{3}$, giving $1.1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.
